mstts:express-as.prosody: Let’s talk about something we all face at some point—holding on to hope and faith when answers are slow. There are times in life when it feels like our prayers just echo back to us, when hope is a thin thread, and faith gets stretched by long, quiet stretches of waiting. If you’re a parent, you probably know this feeling all too well. The longing for change, the waiting for a breakthrough, the fear that maybe nothing will shift. I want you to picture a father—someone who’s been praying for his daughter to come back to faith. The years go by, and on the surface, nothing’s changed. Their conversations are polite, but there’s a distance. He wonders, "Are my prayers even making a difference? Is hope just a dream I’m chasing?" But here’s the thing—he keeps at it. He prays, he believes, he loves. And then, out of the blue, his daughter calls. She shares she’s started going to a church near her place. The journey isn’t finished, but something new is starting. Most parents come to realize that real faith doesn’t just show up when things are easy or answers come fast. No, faith is actually built up in the waiting, in those silent seasons. It’s easy to believe when you can see change happening. But the kind of faith that lasts? That’s grown through persistence—through refusing to give up, even when you can’t see any progress. Take another story—a mom who’s praying for her son, hoping he’ll find direction after a string of tough breaks. She learns to celebrate the little things: a new job, a good friend, a spark of purpose. Each of those moments is a sign—progress is happening, even if it’s slow. She starts to trust that every prayer is heard, every hope matters, every single tear is seen. The waiting? It’s hard. There’s always this urge to give up, to let go, to stop believing. But here’s something to remember—prayer is an act of hope against despair. It’s a way of saying, “The story isn’t over. Change is still possible. Love won’t fail.” Through those long nights and silent days, parents find out that hope isn’t just a feeling—it’s a choice. It’s choosing to keep praying, keep believing, keep loving, no matter what. And there’s a quiet strength in knowing that every prayer, every step of faith, every moment of hope is part of something bigger. The journey keeps going, and the story’s still being written. But as you lean on prayer, you start to realize you’re not alone. Your love matters. Your faith? It can move mountains—even when the answers take their time.
